pick.headline: Terry Waite and Thomas Sutherland freed in Lebanon
pick.summary: On November 18, 1991, Terry Waite, the Archbishop of Canterbury's envoy, and Thomas Sutherland, an American dean at the American University of Beirut, were released after years as hostages in Lebanon.
pick.significance: Waite had been seized in 1987 while negotiating for hostages, and his contacts with Oliver North made him a figure in the Iran-Contra story. The releases were part of a UN-brokered winding up of the Lebanon hostage crisis.
pick.fbis: AFP reported from Beirut on November 18 that Islamic Jihad had announced the release of Terry Waite and Thomas Sutherland; FBIS carried it the same day.

alternates.headline: Vukovar falls to the Yugoslav army
alternates.summary: On November 18, 1991, the Croatian town of Vukovar fell to the Yugoslav People's Army and Serb forces after a siege of nearly three months.
alternates.significance: The destruction of Vukovar and the killing of prisoners afterwards became emblems of the Yugoslav wars.
alternates.fbis: Radio Croatia reported on November 18 that the Yugoslav army commander had written to the EC ambassador in Zagreb about security for EC observers in Vukovar.
